title: Verify the module and file bounds the Pipeline enforces: what is valid for agents and for large projects, and does the product implement it
goal: PO REQUEST 2026-11-19 and PO EXCEPTION FROM THE MODEL DEFAULT (model claude-fable-5-2, maximum effort): the Pipeline enforces, for the projects it governs, a blocking 1000-line limit per hand-written source file, exactly-one-module ownership with declared dependencies, and (advisory only) a 500-line file budget and a 2500-line module budget. These figures were inherited and never analysed. The PO doubts that 1000 lines is an agent-suited bound (too low may produce far too many files, imports and navigation steps, which also confuses an agent) and wants the bounds and the module cut verified for REAL LARGE projects, for example a business system such as a CRM with many bounded contexts (hundreds of thousands to millions of lines), not for the small repository the product is built in. This is the FIRST step; the remediation of the Pipeline's own source (backlog item backlog/items/2026-11-19-the-pipeline-does-not-meet-the-module-and-size-rules-it-imposes-on-projects.md) waits for it and will be planned afterwards against the bounds you recommend. DELIVERABLE: ONE new markdown document, specs/sprint-alfred-epic/plans/architecture-bounds-verification-2026-11-19.md, in English, no code change anywhere. INPUTS: (1) the external research digest specs/sprint-alfred-epic/plans/c33/external-research-digest-2026-11-19.md, collected by the Elephant because you have no web tools: its sources are marked [opened], [search only] or [secondary]; treat [opened] figures as 'as reported by a fetch with a small summarising model' and everything else as unverified; you cannot open the web, so you may use only the digest and your own knowledge, and you must mark every claim that rests on your own recollection rather than on the digest as 'from memory, unverified' and never invent a citation, an author, a figure or a study; (2) the product as implemented, read from the real checkout: plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/architecture-boundary-check.mjs (DEFAULT_LINE_BOUND, the rules, MANAGED_EXCLUSIONS, test-file and generated-file exemptions, exceptions and ratchets), architecture/boundary-policy.json, architecture/fitness-model.json, plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/architecture-fitness.mjs (evaluateSizeBudgets, DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_LINES, DEFAULT_MAX_MODULE_LINES), plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/module-inventory.mjs and the map format (architecture/map/index.md, architecture/map/schemas.md as a small concept file, architecture/map/pipeline-core.md as the very large one: measure it), plugins/pipeline-core/lib/architecture-design.mjs and the design review (how modules are proposed and checked at design time), the dispatch briefing (plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/dispatch-briefing.mjs and templates/prompts/goldfish-task.md: how one module becomes one agent's write scope and context), docs/usage.md, plugins/pipeline-core/skills/pipeline-start/references/happy-path.md, design-course.md, templates/prd.md and plugins/pipeline-core/agents/readiness-reviewer.md for what users and agents are told about modules and size, docs/operating-model.md, docs/adr/README.md (ADRs on modular design and size budgets, for example the draft on modular design by default with size budgets), and the backlog item above (re-measure anything you rely on with plain rg and git reads and with plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/architecture-boundary-check.mjs --root . --json). QUESTIONS THE DOCUMENT MUST ANSWER: (a) What do the digest and your own knowledge really support about file size, module size and module count for agent-assisted work and for large modular systems, separated into established, plausible, contested and absent evidence, with the digest source id for each claim? Is a single numeric line limit supported at all, and which alternative instruments are better supported (kind-aware ranges for entry point, library, test, generated and data files; a context-cost measure in tokens; cognitive-complexity or function-level limits; coupling and dependency rules at module level; report-only at file level and enforce at module and dependency level)? (b) What module cut rule makes sense for agents (what makes a module, target size in lines and in agent-context tokens, a maximum number of allowed dependencies, public interface versus internals, how many modules an agent must be able to hold in its map, how a feature that crosses modules is cut into dispatches, how a very large module is subdivided, how ownership and the existing one-module write scope behave)? (c) Does the product as implemented hold for a large project: for each of the blocking 1000-line rule, the advisory 500-line and 2500-line budgets, the exceptions and ratchets, the one-concept-file-per-module map (read cost of the index and of one concept file at 20 to 60 modules; the 75 KB single concept file of the Pipeline's own core module shows what happens), the design-time module proposal, the module write scope per dispatch and the generated overview: state what works, what breaks at scale and what is inconsistent (for example two different file numbers, a module budget far below any real business module), each with the file and constant as evidence. (d) A recommendation with numbers: for each file kind a recommended range and a default (enforce or report), the module-level rules and numbers, what stays configurable per project and per file kind, how the defaults are justified when the evidence is weak (say plainly that a number is a judgement, give the reasoning and the way to calibrate it from a project's own measurements), and what the Pipeline's own source would look like against them (re-measure: files and lines over the recommended bounds). (e) A CRM-scale worked example: about 20 to 40 modules, 0.5 to 2 million lines, several teams: the module cut, sizes, allowed-dependency graph shape, the map the agent reads, the context an agent receives for one dispatch and its token size, a cross-module feature split into dispatches, what the boundary check would report and how the product should keep that readable. (f) What would have to change in the product to enforce exactly that: the files, rules, defaults, schemas, map format, documentation and agent instructions that change, and for each change whether it alters an existing digest-bound record, a map or policy a user repository already has, or a published default (the PO's central risk for any later rebuild is NEW DRIFT AND NEW STATUS PROBLEMS in user repositories: say what a user repository on an older plugin version sees, and propose a change that is additive, read-compatible and never blocks a repository that is green today; a refusal needs a repair the agent or the PO can run). (g) The decisions only the PO can take, each with your recommendation, and the list of things you could NOT verify. WHAT THE DOCUMENT MUST CONTAIN: the seven headings exactly: '## A. Evidence', '## B. Module cut and file-size principles', '## C. The product as implemented', '## D. Recommendation', '## E. CRM-scale worked example', '## F. Product changes and compatibility', '## G. Decisions and unverified items'. QUALITY BAR: every claim about the product names its file and, where possible, the function or constant; every claim about evidence names its digest source id or says 'from memory, unverified'; numbers are counted, not estimated, and a recommended number is labelled as a judgement with its reasoning; a short, well-supported document beats a long one that mixes guesses with facts; do not defend the 1000-line limit and do not attack it, find what is supported. HARD LIMITS: no change to any file other than the deliverable and the check file; no private consumer project or feature name and no machine path anywhere (neutral ids only, repo-relative paths); do not propose to weaken, skip or auto-approve any gate, signature, push approval or Critic evidence.
